items.name: Readability
items.evidence: No comments explain the odd branches. `except AttributeError: domain = '%s' % DNS_NAME if DNS_NAME is not None else None` is hard to follow, and get_fqdn re-checks `self._fqdn.encode('ascii')` right after converting it, with no reason given.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The same try/encode('ascii')/except/encode('idna') block is pasted three times: twice in CachedDnsName.get_fqdn (the second copy is redundant) and once in message.py. There is no shared helper, and message.py has a branch that only exists to handle string mocks of DNS_NAME.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Exceptions caught are specific (UnicodeEncodeError), but `except AttributeError` is used to guess whether DNS_NAME is a mock. That can hide real AttributeErrors raised inside get_fqdn. Nothing is silently swallowed.

items.name: Conversion is encoding-independent and safe for ASCII names
items.name_zh: 转换与编码无关且不影响 ASCII 主机名
items.evidence: Conversion happens at the source (get_fqdn), works for every email.encoding, and leaves ASCII hostnames unchanged. However, the same idna conversion is repeated inline in get_fqdn (twice) and again at the make_msgid call site, and part of it exists only for test mocks.
